archetype.name: Dual-Threat (scramble-first)
archetype.definition: A quarterback whose rushing value comes mostly from breaking the pocket and scrambling for first downs rather than from called runs, paired with a passing game that wins between the numbers.

report.headline: Accuracy is back and the legs still pay, but sacks are holding him back
report.take:
Daniels is a scramble-first dual-threat. His rushing production is unplanned: 19 scrambles have gone for 212 yards and 10 first downs at 0.846 EPA apiece, while his four designed runs have produced nothing. That is why he leads all qualifying quarterbacks with 53.3 rushing yards a game even as the run game around him ranks 21st. The legs are the floor. What is new this year is the arm. His CPOE sits at 6.44, fourth in the league, a 9.2-point swing from last year's -2.7, and his bad-throw rate is down 3.5 points.

The passing still grades out ordinary, exactly league average at 0.034 EPA per dropback, because two things cancel the accuracy gains. The first is sacks. His 7.9% sack rate ranks 32nd, and he has been hit or sacked on 15.9% of dropbacks behind a line that ranks 27th in hits allowed. The second is the short game. Throws behind the line have cost 10.1 EPA, which leaves everything under 10 air yards at a flat 0.025 a play despite 74% completions. The rest of the tree is excellent: 0.514 EPA a throw in the 10-19 range with a 22.4 CPOE, and positive value even on deep shots he completes under a third of the time.

The numbers also hide some flattering context. His best passing splits come trailing by nine or more (0.244 EPA, 78.4% completions), and a 26th-ranked defense has put him there often. In one-score situations he has been below water at -0.073. Third downs are a real problem: -0.169 EPA and a 30.3% conversion rate. He is facing 8.8 yards to go on average, and five of his ten sacks came on third down. Zero interceptions on 116 attempts will not hold, since his bad-throw rate is still 10.3%. One positive on the sack issue: his pressure-to-sack rate has fallen to 27.3% from the 41-44% range of his first two seasons, so the sacks look more like a line-and-down-distance problem than a habit.

The trajectory is good. His CPOE has climbed every game, peaking at 17.6 with 300 yards against a top-five 49ers defense. Last year's dip now reads as a blip, and his 2024 level (0.204 EPA a play, ninth) is back in view if the protection and the screen game stop leaking. The short-term complication is McLaurin's knee, which takes away one of his two most productive targets.

strengths.title: Scrambles that move the chains
strengths.body: His rushing value comes from improvisation. Scrambles have produced 10 first downs and close to a point of EPA each, while called runs have been stuffed half the time. This has been his identity since he ranked second in rushing yards as a rookie, so the floor is durable, though the volume swings with how often the pocket breaks down.

strengths.title: Accuracy rebound, especially intermediate
strengths.body: His CPOE ranks fourth and is up more than nine points on last year, and his bad-throw rate is down too. The intermediate window is where it shows: 0.514 EPA a throw on 23 attempts with completions far above expectation. That split is a small sample, but the steady game-by-game climb in CPOE and the 2024 baseline both say the accuracy is mostly real.

strengths.title: Fewer sacks once pressured
strengths.body: His pressure-to-sack rate has dropped to 27.3%, after ranking near the bottom of the league at roughly 41-44% in each of his first two seasons. He is getting the ball out or getting out of trouble more often when the rush arrives. That points to a real change in pocket management rather than noise.

concerns.title: Sacks and hits erase the accuracy
concerns.body: A 7.9% sack rate, 32nd of 45, plus nearly one dropback in six ending in a hit or sack, is why his EPA per dropback sits only at league average. The cause is mostly structural: the line ranks 27th in hit rate and he faces long third downs. Over his last three games the sack rate has actually worsened to 9.9%.

concerns.title: Dead short game and third downs
concerns.body: Passes behind the line have cost 10.1 EPA, dragging his entire under-10 game to roughly zero. On third down he is converting under a third of the time against long distances. Both are partly scheme and line, given the screens, the stuffs and the 8.8 yards to go, but they are why a 69.5% passer in recent weeks is adding almost no passing EPA.

concerns.title: Zero picks won't last
concerns.body: No interceptions on 116 attempts leads the league, but his 10.3% bad-throw rate and one turnover-worthy fumble say some luck is involved. He threw nine interceptions in 2024. Expect a few to show up, though the accuracy gains should keep him well below last year's rate.

trend.note: His CPOE has improved every game (-3.4, 3.5, 8.1, 17.6), capped by a 300-yard outing against the fifth-ranked 49ers defense. Rushing has swung with the pass rush, peaking at 103 yards and two scores in the five-sack Giants game.

nextGame.headline: Rested, at home, against a pass rush that rarely gets home
nextGame.body:
Philadelphia attacks the one thing holding Daniels back least of anyone in the league. The Eagles rank 32nd in QB hit rate and 31st in sack rate, so the pocket should be cleaner than usual. They are also 24th against the pass overall and 28th in EPA allowed to opposing WR1s. Where they do hold up is deep, ninth by EPA, which matters little for a passer whose damage comes in the intermediate range. Daniels saw them in Week 1: 164 yards and two touchdowns, with a positive 3.9 passing EPA despite shaky accuracy. He arrives off a bye with 13 days of rest, and no line had been posted yet.

Availability tilts it further. Edge rushers Jalyx Hunt (out) and Nolan Smith Jr. (concussion), plus slot corner Michael Carter II, were all sidelined last week. Their listed return dates precede this game, so treat that as uncertain rather than banked. On offense, Philadelphia has lost Jalen Hurts for the season, Saquon Barkley is out, and Lane Johnson and Landon Dickerson are missing from the line. An already 28th-ranked offense should struggle to build a lead, which means fewer comeback-mode dropbacks for Daniels but more neutral-script snaps. On his side, McLaurin's knee carries an estimated return of game day itself, so his status is a genuine question. If he sits, Diggs becomes the WR1 against a defense that has let that role run wild, and the backfield loses Croskey-Merritt to injured reserve.

keyMatchups.title: Pocket versus a toothless rush
keyMatchups.body: Daniels' sacks stem from a leaky line and long down-and-distance. Philadelphia generates the fewest hits and nearly the fewest sacks in the league. If that holds, his top-five accuracy should finally show up in EPA instead of being taxed by negative plays.

keyMatchups.title: Diggs at the WR1 spot
keyMatchups.body: Diggs leads the team in target EPA. The Eagles allow 0.54 EPA a play to WR1s, 28th in the league, and he likely sees that role whether or not McLaurin plays. Philadelphia is stingy against WR3s, so volume should concentrate on Diggs and Okonkwo.

keyMatchups.title: Game script without Hurts
keyMatchups.body: Washington's defense has kept Daniels trailing, which inflated his passing efficiency in catch-up mode. A Hurts-less Eagles offense ranks 31st in success rate, so this may be a tighter, lower-volume game. That is the setting where his one-score EPA has been negative.

nextGame.watch: Whether his sack rate drops against the league's weakest pass rush: if it does, the accuracy gains should finally show up in his EPA.

restOfSeason.body:
The accuracy looks sustainable. It has climbed steadily, held up against a top-five defense and matches his 2024 profile, and the scramble value is a three-year trait. What should regress is the interception-free run and some of the trailing-script passing efficiency. The red-zone touchdown rate is also generous, with five scores on 45.8% completions inside the 20. The swing variable is protection: his pocket management has improved, so a healthier line or a softer stretch of pass rushes would turn league-average EPA into top-12 production quickly.

Expect roughly 190-240 passing yards and 1.0-1.6 touchdowns a game with 40-60 rushing yards. Rushing touchdowns will come in bunches rather than steadily. Without McLaurin, the targets beyond Diggs and Okonkwo thin out: Burks has been negative, and Antonio Williams' huge per-target number rests on 11 looks. With Mariota also hurt, there is no cushion behind Daniels at quarterback.
swingFactors: Whether the screen game stops bleeding EPA

confidence.note: Only four logged games and small depth splits, but the accuracy trend is consistent and the rushing trait has held for three seasons.
